parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hi, Magda. How was your placement?

It went really well. The kids really enjoyed the science I did with them.

So did mine. I think they found it very motivating.

Yes. The programme we had to teach was much better than the old-style science experiments we did at school.

Yes, though, I don’t understand why the children should have to build a model of a steam engine. I tried it with the kids, but I couldn’t get it to work.

Me neither. And it really shows it’s hard to get any real results.

Yes. And it’s usually the children’s parents, rather than the kids themselves, who favour that type of experiment. So what experiments did you do?

Well, one day a discussion started in class about breakfast cereals, about which one was best. One child then said that we should test them in class.

That’s a nice idea.

Yes. And it wasn’t expensive. We brought four different brands of cereal and had everyone evaluate them for taste, appearance and sogginess in milk.

And are you going to tell me which one won?

No. I’ll let you do it yourself. It obviously isn’t difficult to set up.

Another experiment we did, the sports teacher's idea, actually was to spend a morning seeing how high various balls bounced. For example, do new tennis balls bounce higher than old ones? And do basketballs that are fully inflated bounce better than flatter ones?

And I guess you got some interesting data?

We did. And they had to make a chart to plot the results. It really improved their grasp of charts and graphs and calculation. Apparently, they’d had problems understanding the point of graphs in the past.

Did all your experiments work out okay?

Well, we had one lesson on making paper from grass. The children made a terrible mess in the classroom. Whatever they did didn’t work. And it wasn’t because it was difficult. I think it was because it didn’t engage them at all. It didn’t seem to motivate them.

My tie-dyeing experiment went well. They had to get a piece of material and twist it into a rope and then dye it. The children did end up with blue and green hands for a few days, though.

But don’t you need to spend more than one lesson on that?

Yes, we did it over three classes. The children really loved it, though, and one suggested we make scarves from the result. I declined, as my sewing skills aren’t up to much.

I guess the one experiment that everyone loved in my class was making glue from milk. I thought it would be a complete failure, but in fact, it worked brilliantly. One reason I suspect is that they got feedback straight away. Some children get really restless if they have to wait for anything interesting to happen.

Yes, I think that’s always a good idea. Really helps to make it a success.

I see you've got a diagram there for one of your experiments.

Yes, it was an idea I got from the internet. It was very easy and straightforward to set up. The idea is to make a condenser to extract essences from plants. The large container is made of metal.

Right, and that holds the hot water.

That's right, and it has a strainer which sits inside it. This is where you put the plant matter. We used plants like rosemary as the essence you can extract is quite strong.

So what's the container right at the top?

It's made of glass. It's where we put the ice. The glass container has a drip tip at the bottom.

What's that for?

It's where the essence collects.

Where does the essence go then?

Into the dish at the bottom. It's made of pottery.

Sounds good. I might try it with my class.

analyses.content: 两人都表示虽然尝试了制作蒸汽机模型，但是“没能让它运转起来”（couldn't get it to work），并总结说很难得到真正的结果。
Magda: I tried it with the kids, but I couldn't get it to work. Speaker: Me neither. And it really shows it’s hard to get any real results.
听到 "couldn't get it to work" 和 "hard to get any real results" 对应选项 B。
Magda: Yes. And it wasn't expensive. We brought four different brands of cereal...
"Wasn't expensive" 直接对应选项 G "cheap to do"。
Magda 说这个实验并不贵（wasn't expensive），她们买了几种不同的麦片，这就意味着成本低。
Speaker: It really improved their grasp of charts and graphs and calculation.
"Improved their grasp of charts and graphs and calculation" 对应选项 F 中的 "maths"。
这个实验要求学生制作图表来绘制结果，实际上提高了学生对图表、图形和计算（calculation）的掌握能力。
Magda: I think it was because it didn’t engage them at all. It didn’t seem to motivate them.
"Didn't engage them" 和 "Didn't seem to motivate them" 对应选项 A。Magda 明确排除了 "difficult"（不是因为难），所以不选 B。
Magda 认为这个实验失败不是因为难，而是因为根本没有吸引到学生（didn't engage them at all），没有激励作用，即无聊。 (注：题目图片中选项 A 印成了 "very boning"，实为 "very boring" 的印刷错误)
Speaker: But don’t you need to spend more than one lesson on that? Magda: Yes, we did it over three classes.
"More than one lesson" 和 "over three classes" 对应选项 H "takes longer than usual"。
男生问是不是需要花不止一节课的时间，Magda 确认说她们用了三节课才完成（over three classes）。
Magda 认为这个实验非常成功，因为学生们立刻得到了反馈（got feedback straight away），不需要等待。
Magda: One reason I suspect is that they got feedback straight away.
"Straight away" 对应选项 E "immediate"。
Magda: The large container is made of metal.
图中 D 指向最外层的大容器，下方有 "Hot water" 的标识，符合描述。
Magda 介绍说那个大的容器（The large container）是金属做的，用来装热水。
Magda: That's right, and it has a strainer which sits inside it.
图中 F 指向位于大容器内部、盛放植物（图中那一堆小东西）的网状部件。
Magda 说大容器里面坐着一个滤网（strainer which sits inside it），用来放植物材料。
Magda: The glass container has a drip tip at the bottom.
图中 A 是顶部的玻璃容器，而 G 明确指向该容器底部凸起的尖头部分。
顶部的玻璃容器（glass container）底部有一个滴液尖头（drip tip）。
Magda: Into the dish at the bottom. It's made of pottery.
图中 C 指向位于滤网内部、正对着滴液尖头下方的小碗/碟子，用来收集液体。
精华液（essence）最终会滴落到底部的碟子里，那个碟子是陶制的（made of pottery）。
